puzzles.title: Bruno
puzzles.scenario: Bruno was the only name in the will. Bruno couldn't read, couldn't sign, and was murdered the day after the funeral.
puzzles.solution: Bruno was the dead woman's dog. She left her fortune to him, on the condition that it would pass to her son the moment he died. Her son didn't wait for a natural death — he poisoned the dog food. The instant Bruno died, he inherited everything.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask who Bruno was to the family. Ask what he was.

puzzles.title: Lifesaver
puzzles.scenario: Fien's smoke detector once saved her life. A year later, that same smoke detector killed her.
puzzles.solution: The detector's battery had been chirping for days. Her husband, who had wanted her dead without a trace for months, waited until she climbed onto the kitchen chair to replace it herself. At the right moment, he pushed her off. She fell, and no one ever saw a weapon.
puzzles.hint: Don't look at who came in. Look at what was already hanging from the ceiling.

puzzles.title: Prince
puzzles.scenario: Prince was disabled overnight. An hour later, the villa's safe was empty.
puzzles.solution: Prince wasn't the guard dog — it was the nickname of the security system, named after the owner's late dog. An ex-technician who had installed the system himself knew exactly which wire to cut. He'd wired it in the first place.
puzzles.hint: Prince didn't need to breathe to be switched off.

puzzles.title: Fire Drill
puzzles.scenario: During the office's annual fire drill, one employee died for real that afternoon.
puzzles.solution: The drill was fake, but the emergency exit wasn't: it had been jammed for months by new carpet laid under the door that no one had trimmed back. During the drill, the crowd pushed too hard toward that one exit. One coworker was crushed underneath. The drill was fake. The death was real.
puzzles.hint: Ask about the emergency exit, not the fire.

puzzles.title: The Intern
puzzles.scenario: The alarm had already gone off five times that night. On the sixth, no one responded — and the guard was murdered.
puzzles.solution: A new intern had been testing the freshly installed alarm system over and over that evening, without telling the control room. When the break-in was real, the control room assumed it was another glitch and ignored it. The guard faced the burglars completely alone. No one came, because everyone thought it was another false alarm.
puzzles.hint: How many times had the alarm already gone off that night, and why?

puzzles.title: The Vault Thief
puzzles.scenario: For two years, exactly one fifty-euro note has gone missing from the company safe, always on the third of the month.
puzzles.solution: The safe sits right next to the boiler. During monthly maintenance, the technician opens the safe room to reach the pipes. For two years, without anyone noticing, he's taken exactly one note each time as his own little 'tip.' He never once called it theft.
puzzles.hint: Who's legally allowed near the safe, with their own key, without it counting as theft?

puzzles.title: Mr. Grey
puzzles.scenario: Mr. Grey had sat on the same courtroom bench for forty years, until he was found dead there one morning. No one knew his last name.
puzzles.solution: Mr. Grey was no judge, lawyer, or defendant — he was a homeless man who had used the courtroom for decades as a warm, safe place during the day. The bailiff only ever knew him by that nickname, and never asked for more. He died exactly where he felt safest.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask what his role in the courtroom was. Ask whether he had one at all.

puzzles.title: The Star Witness
puzzles.scenario: The only witness who could confirm the charge against a criminal died the day before the trial — struck by lightning.
puzzles.solution: There was no hitman, no conspiracy. During a storm, the witness crossed an open field to reach his car and was simply struck by lightning, on the one day that actually mattered for the case. The case didn't collapse because of a crime. It collapsed because of the weather.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask who wanted the witness silenced. Ask whether anyone actually did.
